about.title: Redwood City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Redwood City sits along the US-101 corridor on the Peninsula, and the local numbers reflect steady, everyday traffic. The 2025 public record lists 305 injury collisions inside the city, with 412 people hurt and one life lost. Collision counts point to US-101, Woodside Road, El Camino Real, and Middlefield Road as the corridors where the most crashes get reported, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. show the highest concentration. If you were one of those 412 people, the days after a collision can feel oddly quiet at first and then suddenly crowded: adjusters calling, forms arriving, a car sitting in a tow yard. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Redwood City car accident claims on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless your case recovers money. You talk with a lawyer, ask your questions, and decide what happens next.

whyChoose.title: Why Redwood City Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: The clock in California is real
items.desc: Most car accident claims here carry a two-year filing deadline, but a claim involving a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can tell you quickly which deadline applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a collision on Middlefield Road, you can still pursue the share that belongs to the other driver. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage.

items.title: Contingency fees and no damage cap
items.desc: The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is nothing to pay up front and no fee unless there is a recovery. California also places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car accident case.

items.question: My crash was on US-101 in Redwood City. Who do I get the report from?
items.answer: Collisions on the freeway itself are usually handled by the California Highway Patrol, while crashes on surface streets like Woodside Road or El Camino Real are typically taken by Redwood City police. If you are unsure which agency responded, note the officer's agency from any card or paperwork you were handed. An attorney can request the report for you and pull it into the claim.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink your claim. Keep your own records instead: photos of the vehicles and the scene, the names of witnesses, and every medical visit.

items.question: What evidence should I hold on to after a Redwood City collision?
items.answer: Save everything, even things that seem minor: photos of the damage, the tow receipt, repair estimates, urgent-care paperwork, and any dashcam or phone video. Nearby businesses along El Camino Real or Middlefield Road may have camera footage that gets overwritten within days, so an attorney will often send preservation requests early. Write down your own account of the crash while it is still fresh.
